sections.heading: A PRACTICAL COMPARISON
sections.body:
Imagine a Soldier
Armor of God - The soldier's equipment. Without armor, he becomes vulnerable.
Fruit of the Spirit - The soldier's character. Without character, he becomes unstable.
Gifts of the Spirit - The soldier's abilities and assignments. Without gifts, he becomes ineffective.
Armor protects him.
Fruit shapes him.
Gifts use him.

sections.heading: CONCLUSION
sections.body:
Many Christians focus on one area while neglecting the others. God desires believers to be:
 Protected through the Armor of God
 Transformed through the Fruit of the Spirit
 Empowered through the Gifts of the Spirit
A mature believer should possess all three.

sections.heading: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
sections.body:
1. Which of the three areas do you focus on most?
2. Which area do you tend to neglect?
3. Can someone have spiritual gifts without spiritual maturity?
4. How do the Armor, Fruit, and Gifts work together in the life of a believer?
Closing Thought

The Armor of God helps us stand.
The Fruit of the Spirit helps us grow.
The Gifts of the Spirit help us serve.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the armor of God?
quiz.explanation: Ephesians 6:11 — to stand against the wiles of the devil.

quiz.question: What is the fruit of the Spirit meant to produce?
Why are spiritual gifts given according to 1 Corinthians 12:7?
quiz.explanation: Gifts build up the body of Christ.

quiz.question: In the soldier analogy, what does the fruit of the Spirit represent?
quiz.explanation: Fruit shapes who the believer is becoming.

quiz.question: What does a mature believer need according to this study?
options: Only one of the three areas
quiz.explanation: God desires believers who are protected, transformed, and empowered.

title: Armor of God, Fruit of the Spirit, Gifts of the Spirit
description: A Back to the Bible study comparing three essential aspects of the Christian life — standing firm, growing in character, and serving others.

passageReading.text:
10 Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.
11 Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
12 For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.
13 Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
14 Stand therefore, having girded your waist with truth, having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
15 and having shod your feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
16 above all, taking the shield of faith with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked one.
17 And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;
